The top now carries what a legal text should: version, last updated and scope. Three things were genuine faults. The text could not be selected and therefore not copied — wrong for a privacy policy you may need to quote from. Sections only faded in while scrolling; if that mechanism stalled you were left with a blank page, so the fade-in has been dropped entirely. And the page now prints properly. On the English version the table of contents had also stayed half German.
changelog_en.4.8.8: ArchFlow now explains itself. The page used to be labelled entirely in English although it lives at a German address, and for search engines it consisted of twelve words, because all of its content is drawn into a graphic where no text exists. Opening it now shows an explanation on the right (a card on phones): what the map shows, what the colours mean, how to operate it and where the data comes from. That text is real page content, visible in both layouts rather than hidden from search engines. The English version at /en/ has been fully translated alongside it. Plus a preview image for shared links, a proper heading structure and a link to the open source code: if a tile looks interesting, you can go straight from there to the real file on GitHub.
changelog_en.4.8.7: The architecture view at /archflow/ has been redesigned from the ground up. Fonts, colours and controls now match the rest of the app, emoji symbols are replaced by drawn icons, and the accent follows the colour you picked. The biggest change is the colour system. Previously 53 groups shared 21 colours, so two neighbouring groups could carry the same one — the colour meant nothing. Now colour means exactly one thing: the kind of file (page, script, style), three validated tones, and a connecting line takes the colour of whatever it pulls in. The legend is built from the data instead of being hard-coded; it used to promise five kinds of link, three of which never occur in this project. The overview was also unusable: showing everything at once landed at 18 percent zoom, where every label was a few pixels tall. Groups are now packed into the available area instead of stacked into a narrow column (34 percent), and zooming out drops the unreadable labels in favour of the structure, bringing names back as you zoom in. Along the way a counting error surfaced: 59 JSON files were listed as JavaScript because the detection was imprecise. The view can now be operated by keyboard, and it links back into the app again.
changelog_en.4.8.6: The architecture view at /archflow/ reflects the actual state of the project again. Its underlying data file was from 18 May and roughly two and a half months out of date — everything added since (multiple jobs, P2P sync, the survey, the English-version tooling) was simply missing from the diagram. After a fresh scan it now holds 226 files and 227 connections instead of 150 and 91. On top of that, the English version of the page never loaded its data: it looked for it at an address that does not exist there and got stuck on the loading bar. Both are fixed, and the analyzer script is back in the project so the view can be refreshed with a single command.
changelog_en.4.8.5: The vocational school view has been redesigned, and two display bugs in it are fixed. The most obvious one: the ring in the top right permanently showed “---” instead of your grade average. The figure was calculated correctly all along, but it was written into the graphic in a way that has no effect there, so it never became visible. The average is there now, coloured by its grade band. Second, a rectangular shadow sat around the ring: the glow around the coloured arc was cut off hard at the edge of the graphic, with two angle marks in the corners on top of that. Both are gone and the ring stands on its own. A third bug turned up along the way: the slim progress bar in the header left out one of the four grade bands entirely and so was never complete. It has been dropped, and the distribution is shown in full in its own panel. The rest is design. The view used to present itself as a technical console: bevelled corners, angle markers, a drifting grid in the background, tiles hanging at staggered heights and labels such as “ACADEMIC INTELLIGENCE”, “LIVE DATA” or “AI INSIGHTS” that explained nothing. It now uses the same quiet presentation as the rest of the application. Under “My subjects”, every grade had its own row labelled “Grade 1”, “Grade 2”, “Grade 3”, which turned into a long list across four subjects. Grades now sit side by side as small fields you can type into directly, with a field at the end for adding another. Rename and delete are icons rather than emoji and are permanently visible, so they can be reached on a phone too. On colour: the grade distribution used four hues for something that is a ranking, including two greens that were hard to tell apart even with full colour vision. Only the bands that report something carry colour now, the middle is neutral, and every row also states its range in figures. Numbers follow the language you have set. The English version is updated along with it.
changelog_en.4.8.4: A follow-up to yesterday's PDF export: it was tidy, but it looked like it came from a different application. Its own typeface, its own colours, rounded boxes — none of it matched the shadow report book you actually see in the program. That is fixed. The record now uses the same type, the same fine dividing lines, the same severity markers and the same timeline with a dot and a line as the app — just on white. The sheet now visibly comes from here. The colours for “critical” and “high” are the app's again: they were recalculated against white paper and hold apart perfectly well there, so a separate print palette was simply unnecessary. Everything that was fixed yesterday in terms of genuine printing bugs stays: the distribution chart still prints, the cover heading no longer breaks out of the margin, the print dialog opens by itself, and the colour-free second level conveyed through border weight still keeps severities apart on a black-and-white printout. New on top of that, the document now waits for its fonts before printing — otherwise the browser briefly printed the fallback typeface and the layout jumped.
changelog_en.4.8.3: The shadow report book's PDF export has been reworked — and along the way three bugs surfaced that only ever existed on paper. The worst: the severity distribution chart was not printed at all. Browsers omit background colours when printing by default, so it came out as an empty grey bar and every colour-filled marker as a white box — while on screen the document looked correct every time. Second, the cover heading ran past the margin and was clipped. Third, the print dialog sometimes never opened, because it hung on a moment that had often already passed by the time it was checked; the document now starts printing itself once it has finished loading, embedded evidence photos included. Also: every page carries the case reference and a “Confidential” note at the top, the distribution shows one row per level with a bar and a count instead of a stacked colour band, and evidence photos are embedded at twice the size — at roughly four centimetres wide, nothing was legible enough to serve as evidence. On top of the colour, the severity marker carries a second, colour-free level through border weight: print the record on a black-and-white printer and the difference between “critical” and “low” is still visible. The closing note states more clearly what the checksum does and does not prove.
changelog_en.4.8.2: The shadow report book has been redesigned from the ground up, in the direction that was asked for twice: less performance, more document. The lock screen used to be a narrow box floating in an otherwise empty black field; on a monitor it looked like a phone view somebody had enlarged. Now the explanation sits on the left and the vault on the right, so what the page is for is visible immediately instead of hidden behind a scroll hint. A lot of repetition went with it: "AES-256 encrypted", a crypto badge, a warning box and a footer line all said the same thing four times over; it is now stated once, where the decision is actually made. The padlock symbol with its crosshair ticks and the permanent CONFIDENTIAL bar are gone — both were props, and the bar cost a full row in every session for something you read once. The biggest change is colour. Each severity level used to carry its own hue (red, amber, blue, teal, grey), with a second, unrelated colour scale running alongside it for the handling status, plus violet category labels and a violet edit button: six colours competing at once. But severity is a ranking, not an assortment — now only the two levels that must stand out carry colour (critical, high), the middle is neutral, and the bottom two differ by shape rather than hue. That was not decided by eye but calculated: the previous tones sat too close together to be told apart reliably on a dark background. Entries are also no longer a loose list of cards but a dated timeline — the book is a chronology, and now it looks like one. The statistics row at the top is one quiet band instead of four coloured tiles, and a zero is no longer painted red, because it is not raising an alarm. Typographically, three foreign typefaces (one of them a condensed poster face used for every heading) have given way to the project's own two, which incidentally loads one font file fewer. On phones the header used to collapse the app name to nothing and the search field was cut off — both fixed, without hiding a single function. The page now also follows your chosen accent colour; red is reserved for status (critical, delete) and stays fixed. The English version is translated along with it.
changelog_en.4.8.1: The device-sync QR code led nowhere on the scanning device. Instead of the pairing dialog you got the app's opening film, the page would not scroll, no field would take input — it looked like a crash. It was not one: anyone scanning a pairing QR is opening MyWorkLog on the second device for the very first time, and the first ever visit plays the intro. That intro covers the whole page and locks scrolling — so the pairing dialog did open, just invisibly behind it. Nothing looked like an error because nothing had failed; there was simply a lid on top. The intro is now skipped whenever the address carries a sync code, taking you straight to the pairing dialog with the code already filled in. The intro is not used up by this: it plays as usual on the next normal visit. Also covered is the case where the code arrives later — Android likes to open scanned links in the tab that is already open, so the page never reloads; if the intro happens to be running there, it is now closed and scrolling is released.
changelog_en.4.8.0: Refinement pass on the shadow report book based on user feedback. First, a category was missing: "Training duty neglected" describes the case "the company trains too little" — but the other, at least equally common case (an apprentice doing warehouse work or errands instead of training content) had no category of its own and was therefore confusingly filed under "neglect". There is now a dedicated tenth category, "Non-training tasks", with its own detail fields (which task, how often) and its own escalation guide. Both category labels are also sharpened ("… too little guidance" vs. "… work unrelated to training"), and the previously vague "Missing since" field is now labelled "Guidance missing since" or "Documentation missing since" — the bare field name used to leave it open whether it referred to missing training content or, say, the apprentice being absent. Second, the design refined in the last update was still too playful for users: the three floating, colour-shimmering background blobs and their endless animation are gone entirely, corner radii are noticeably smaller project-wide (cards/buttons/modals now read as crisper rather than soft and rounded), and the red-to-violet gradients on buttons, card border lines and the page title have given way to a single calm accent colour — red is now reserved for genuine status/alert use (critical, delete), not decoration. Coloured glow shadows on buttons and the critical-entry border line have been dialled back to plain, unobtrusive shadows.
changelog_en.4.7.0: Professionalized the shadow report book, visually and content-wise. Design: the lock screen used to have a rotating "CONFIDENTIAL" film-prop stamp, two endlessly spinning rings on the lock icon, a scanline overlay, and several infinite-loop animations with no information value — all removed. Every vault now gets a real case reference (e.g. "SB-20260728-4F2A"), shown in the header and on the PDF cover page. Every emoji (category icons, severity dots, buttons, toast messages) has been replaced with SVG icons — while doing so, found and fixed a bug where the unlock button permanently lost its icon on click because the loading-state text overwrote it. New under the stat tiles: a severity-distribution bar at a glance. Content-wise: each of the nine categories now has its own detail fields instead of just free text — for overtime, e.g. number of hours, who ordered it and whether compensation was promised; for discrimination, the affected characteristic under German equal-treatment law; for safety violations, the hazard type. Plus a new status field (open/raised/escalated/resolved) for every entry. The PDF export has been rebuilt from a single running document into a proper multi-page record: a cover page with case reference and period, a clickable table of contents (deliberately without invented page numbers — those come from the browser print dialog's "headers and footers" option), a statistics page with severity distribution plus category and status tables, and the incidents themselves now showing the new detail fields and status.
changelog_en.4.6.0: The shadow report book has been brought up to emergency-grade level. Until now the encrypted vault lived only in this one browser's storage — switching devices or clearing browser data meant total loss of exactly the entries you would need most urgently. You can now export the vault (still encrypted) as a file and restore it on another device, including directly from the lock screen. Entries can also carry evidence photos (auto-compressed, still encrypted along with the rest) — shown as a thumbnail on the entry and embedded in the PDF export; if storage is running low you get a warning instead of evidence being silently dropped. There is also a new change history: every edit to an entry saves the previous version instead of overwriting it, and each entry gets a short fingerprint hash — neither claims cryptographic tamper-proofing, but both are visible and traceable in the export. A new vault menu also allows changing your password (previously missing entirely). And when creating an entry, an „Insert template“ button now helps with a fillable who/what/when/where/witnesses skeleton per category, plus a new „Contacts & next steps“ panel that shows, based on the category, who the JAV, chamber-of-commerce training advisory, trade supervisory authority or anti-discrimination agency are for — including a note that this does not replace legal advice.
changelog_en.4.5.1: The cloud AI in the report book generator now runs on a new model chain. Background: OpenRouter shuts free models down without notice, and that is exactly what had happened to two of the previous stages — the large GPT-OSS 120B and the small LFM 1.2B were simply gone. The built-in fallback caught that cleanly, but as a result every request quietly ran on the last and weakest stage: it kept working, the generated weeks just got noticeably worse — precisely the kind of failure nobody reports as a failure. The new order is North Mini Code (Cohere) → Nemotron 3 Nano 30B (NVIDIA) → Laguna M.1 (Poolside) → GPT-OSS 20B (OpenAI). All four were checked against OpenRouter's live list and deliberately come from four different providers, so that one provider going down cannot kill every stage at once again. If a model fails or returns unusable JSON, the next one is called automatically — you will not notice any of it while generating. The info box „How it works: models, prompt, rate limit“ on the report book page lists the new chain, and the internal benchmark page now tests the same four models that run in production.
changelog_en.4.5.0: Custom entry types can now choose their icon. Until now there was only an „Emoji (optional)“ field — and anyone who left it empty got the same grey label symbol for EVERY custom type. Custom types could therefore never look like Work, Vocational school or Vacation, each of which has its own drawn symbol. The Custom tab now has a „Symbol / Emoji“ switch under „Your types“. In symbol mode there are 26 drawn icons to pick from — dumbbell, car, train, plane, house, meeting, coaching, book, code, terminal, server, wrench, hard hat, phone, mail, folder, clipboard, coffee, moon, sun, clock, truck, star and more. The tiles carry the colour you picked for the type and update the moment you choose a different one, so you can see straight away how the type will look in history, charts and the entry form. Emoji mode works exactly as before. Existing types are unchanged — if you had set an emoji it stays, if you had not you keep the symbol. Also fixed along the way: in symbol mode the emoji no longer sneaks in front of the name. Previously it sat there even when no emoji was being shown at all.
changelog_en.4.4.0: Device sync can now be set up with a QR code. Until now the invitation code — 700 to 1100 characters depending on the network — had to reach the other device somehow: typing it is hopeless, so it meant a detour through a messenger or notes app. There is now a „QR code“ button next to „Copy“ that shows the code as an image. The other device simply scans it with its normal camera app and lands straight in MyWorkLog with the code already filled in — no in-app scanner and nothing extra to install. The code sits in the address fragment after the #, so it is never sent to the server, and the app clears it from the address bar right after reading it so it does not linger in history or bookmarks. Said plainly: for the answer code this route only works if the sending device can scan and its invitation is still open there — after a reload the invitation is gone, and the app now says so clearly instead of silently doing nothing. Copying stays the right way in that case, and the hint under the QR code says as much. One find along the way: the QR library was being loaded on EVERY page view even though nothing in the project used it — 19.9 KB for nothing. It is now fetched only when you actually open the QR code.
changelog_en.4.3.1: The Recovery Center — where you bring back earlier states of your data — has been redesigned. It used to be mostly decoration: a pulsing icon, a purple-to-cyan gradient header, three equally sized tiles and a second close button at the bottom doing the same as the X on top. What actually matters in an emergency was nowhere to be seen. That is the point now: saved states are listed as a timeline ordered by age — „just now“, „47 min ago“, „3d ago“ — instead of a calendar date you have to convert in your head. The date is still shown underneath. New, and really the main thing: each state shows how many entries it holds compared to your current state, green with a plus or red with a minus. That tells you which state is the right one without trial and error. The newest one is marked in your accent colour. Buttons now say what they do: „Restore“ replaces your data, „Merge“ only adds missing entries and overwrites nothing. „Load localStorage“ is now „Reload saved data“ — the old name described the plumbing, not the action. Deleting all backups sits apart and in red, because it is the only action here that can destroy something, and it now asks inside the app instead of in the grey browser box. The window follows your accent colour from now on; a second blue was previously hard-coded and never changed along with it.
changelog_en.4.3.0: Two things. First, a silent failure in the report-book AI: of the three language models behind it, the provider had shut down two without notice, including the best one. It never showed up as an error, only as worse suggestions, because the weakest remaining model automatically stepped in. Four current models are configured now, deliberately from three different providers, so one outage cannot take out every fallback at once. Second, something new: a short poll. Time tracking, cloud sync, analytics and the PDF export stay free, none of that changes. The only thing that costs money every month is the AI that writes the report book, and that is exactly what the question is about: would a much stronger AI be worth something to you, one that picks up your writing style, an exam check against the training plan, several weeks in one run, or dropping the daily limit? None of these exist yet; they are ideas. Plus the question of what that would be worth per month. The poll appears from your fifth entry, allows multiple answers, needs no sign-up and can be dismissed; say „no thanks“ and it will not come back. Only those two answers are sent: no name, no email, none of your entries. On top of that, two questions about usage: how often you write your report book today, and how often you would write it if the ticked improvements existed. The second one deliberately comes AFTER the feature list so it is clear what it refers to. The interesting part is not either answer on its own but the gap between them: if someone says „once a week“ today and the same again with the improvements, then the ideas would not be worth their price, whatever the price question says.
changelog_en.4.2.2: Device sync over WebRTC practically never worked: you tapped „Connect devices“, watched a spinner, and then nothing happened. The cause sat in the list of helper servers that look for a route between the two devices. It held three entries from a provider that no longer responds, and because the app waits until ALL servers have answered, that one provider blocked the whole thing. Measured: 22 seconds with those entries, two tenths of a second without them. The dead servers are gone, and more importantly the app now waits at most 5 seconds and then uses whichever routes it has found. If it finds none at all, it says so plainly instead of handing you a code nobody can connect with. That is exactly what used to happen, and why the second device waited forever too. The connection attempt after the reply code gets a time limit as well; before, the button could stay disabled indefinitely because the network layer often reports nothing at all behind strict firewalls. The progress bar was also just pretending: it counted stubbornly up to 90 percent no matter what the connection did, with „Connected to ...“ above it before anything was connected. It now shows the real state, the elapsed time and how many network routes were found. The interface got cleaned up in the same pass: drawn icons instead of emojis, colors taken from your accent instead of hard-coded purple gradients, clear step-by-step labels, and text that says what is happening. The intro line in the Team tab used to promise shared dashboards and live notifications. Neither exists; it now describes what the feature actually does.
changelog_en.4.2.1: The keyboard-shortcuts switch only ever turned off half of them — and shortcuts are now off by default. Behind the scenes two independent shortcut systems were running: one listened to the switch, the other never did. So the app kept reacting to Ctrl+R, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+5, Alt+S, Delete and Ctrl+Space even with the switch off — taking the browser's own shortcuts away from it in the process, reload and find included. Now every shortcut asks the same switch, including Ctrl+K for the command search, Ctrl+B for the sidebar and Ctrl+Shift+K for Ghost Mode. On a fresh install shortcuts are therefore off; you can enable them in Settings under Shortcuts. Anyone who already had them on keeps them exactly as they were. Also fixed: the single keys S, P and E for start, pause and end responded to every key combination as well. So Ctrl+S both saved AND started the timer, Ctrl+E stopped it instead of editing the entry, Alt+S started it instead of collapsing the sidebar, and typing a capital S started it too. Those three keys now only respond when no other key is held. Regardless of the switch, Esc always remains the way out of Ghost Mode — otherwise you would be stuck in it with shortcuts turned off.
changelog_en.4.2.0: A new rule for the version number, plus a bit of code cleanup. Until now every change simply got another digit at the end — which is how the version ended up at 4.1.35, with that last digit set to run on forever. From now on there is a ceiling: once the last digit reaches 19 the middle one moves up, and at 4.9.19 the next whole number follows. That is why this release jumps straight from 4.1.35 to 4.2.0. Content-wise, an old settings dialog for the distribution chart is gone — after a rebuild no button pointed at it any more, and its switches had no effect anyway — which is 108 lines less code. Nothing changes visibly there; the dialog you open via the gear on the bar is unchanged and was always the new one. What is visible is the streak display in the flextime card: it now uses drawn icons instead of emojis. The icon rises with your streak — snowflake at zero, then sprout, flame, star, trophy, rocket — and rotates daily within a tier. Emojis had two problems here: they could not take on your accent color, and they clashed with the drawn balance scale right next to them. The best-streak value also said „Best" twice — once as the label, once inside the value.
changelog_en.4.1.35: On the English site the two chart settings dialogs on the dashboard were still entirely in German — the windows that open when you style the balance trend curve or the working time distribution to your own taste. Everything there is now labeled in English: the chart type (line, area, smooth, bars), line width, line style and data points, the effects (area gradient, glow, rainbow, soft blur), grid, zero line and the animation speed — and likewise the bar settings with bar height, corner radius, segment gap and the display options. The reason for the gap: the app assembles these windows in the browser, so the page's normal translation never reached them. As a side effect the second dialog had ended up half German and half English — that is fixed along with it. The German page is unchanged.
changelog_en.4.1.34: The Shadow Report Book is now fully in English on /en/ too. The page frame was already translated, but the actual app runs in JavaScript and therefore stayed German: the category and severity labels, all messages (vault created/locked, entry saved/deleted), the empty states, the entry form and the lock screen. The exported complaint record (TXT and PDF) is now generated in English on the English page as well — with translated headings, incident blocks, witnesses, signature line and notice text. The statute/chamber abbreviations (IHK, AES-256) stay as they are. The German page is unchanged.
changelog_en.4.1.33: The Rights Checker (/en/rechte-checker/) is now fully in English. Until now only the page frame was translated — the actual content all lives in JavaScript and therefore stayed German: all 51 scenarios with their title, verdict, the cited sections from the BBiG, JArbSchG, ArbZG and others, the practical tips and the ready-made email template to the boss. All of that is newly translated (the statute abbreviations stay German because they are the real laws). Search now understands English terms too (e.g. 'overtime', 'bullying', 'sick on holiday'), and the category names, verdict labels, the AI legal advisor including its messages and the structured data for Google are in English. German rules apply to English-speaking apprentices as well — now they can actually read them. The German page is unchanged.
changelog_en.4.1.32: Two things straightened out on the English site. First a mistake of mine: single words such as “Saldo” or “Berufsschule“ were also replaced where the rest of the text was still German — producing “balance anpassen” or “Zieladresse (Betrieb / Vocational school)”. Half-translated is worse than not translated, so single words are now only replaced where the context is unambiguous. Second, newly translated: the balance adjustment dialog, the weather card (feels like, humidity), the cloud button, the export message and the commuting-costs page with its transport modes, address fields and ticket links.
changelog_en.4.1.31: More English gaps closed, mostly on the dashboard: the entire side navigation (History, Commuting costs, Year view, Month view, Trash, Warnings, Guide …), the balance trend card (direction and volatility), the vacation tile, the voice button in the entry form and the app-generated entry texts in the history and tooltips (“Manual (8.5h)”, “Vocational school – Wednesday (6.75h of lessons → 8.75h credited)”, sick note, vacation day). They were found with a new method: the German and English pages are compared string by string, and anything identical is suspect. The previous search for German words had missed terms without umlauts such as “Stimme” or “Urlaubsstunden”.
changelog_en.4.1.30: Follow-up to the English translation: the greeting in the dashboard header was still German (“Guten Abend, …”). It now switches to English depending on the time of day, while your name is of course left untouched. The tooltip on the weather icon next to it is translated as well.
changelog_en.4.1.29: The English site is now genuinely English. Until now only text baked into the HTML was translated, but the bulk of the interface is generated in the browser and therefore stayed German: page titles, tooltips, weekday and month names, date formats, KPI wording, empty states, the yearly review, the weather card, the public holiday names and the footer. Measured in a running browser that was 555 German spots; there are none left. Date and number formats follow the language too (24/07/2026 instead of 24.07.2026), and the changelog appears in English. The German site is unchanged. The report book's phrasing suggestions deliberately stay German — they go into the official training record, where English would simply be wrong.
changelog_en.4.1.28: The shadow report book was practically invisible to Google: no description, no canonical address, not in the sitemap and — apart from the password screen — not a single readable sentence. There is now a proper page underneath the vault: what a shadow report book actually is, how it differs from the official one, what apprentices record in it, how the encryption works and the most common questions about it. On top of that come complete page details for search engines and social networks, structured data for the question display in Google search, the sitemap entry and the shared footer. The page is now also available in English at /en/schatten-berichtsheft/.
changelog_en.4.1.27: The data safety reminder can now be dismissed: one click on “Don't show this again” hides it everywhere at once — no matter whether you dismiss it on the dashboard, in the settings, in the cloud tab or in the recovery centre. You can bring it back any time via the new “Data safety reminder” switch in the settings under Profile.
changelog_en.4.1.26: New: a quiet reminder about backing up your data — at the foot of the dashboard, in the settings below the recovery centre, in the cloud tab and in the recovery centre itself. Your entries live exclusively in your local browser; there is no copy of them and therefore nobody who could restore them if the browser storage is lost. During testing exactly that happened a few times for no apparent reason, and the cause is still open. The reminder says so openly and points straight to the two ways to protect yourself: download a backup or turn on cloud sync. Deliberately understated — no popup, no alarm.
changelog_en.4.1.25: The entry-type emojis are now gone everywhere, not just in the entry form: the history list and filter pills, dashboard activities, entry details, entry editing, delete dialogs, the recycle bin, the balance-trend tooltip and the type manager in the settings all show the same clean symbol in the colour of the type. The edit window received the same picker as the entry form. Tidied up along the way: the activities card existed twice in the code and had already drifted apart, and the type colours lived in four tables that contradicted each other — vocational school was cyan instead of blue in the history, public holidays pink instead of amber. Every colour now comes from the type itself, which finally makes custom entry types consistently colourful too. An emoji for custom types is optional from now on: without one, the type gets a symbol in your colour.
changelog_en.4.1.24: When creating an entry, the type picker still showed emojis in front of Work, Vocational school, Vacation and the other types. A native select can only display text, so it became a real picker: every type now has a clean symbol in its own type colour — the same colour as in the distribution chart. Operable with mouse, finger and keyboard (arrow keys, Enter, Esc). A custom emoji on your own entry types is preserved, that is your data. Along the way, the gear in the setup hint and the calendar symbol in the vacation hint became symbols instead of emojis, and type names are finally translated on the English site.
changelog_en.4.1.23: The hint that appears on your first visit to the report book page could only be dismissed after twelve seconds. That was too long — it is now five.
changelog_en.4.1.22: Until now the shadow report book could only be found by clicking the heading of the report book page five times in quick succession — so, in practice, not at all. There is now a dedicated section at the bottom of the report book page that above all explains why it exists: your report book is signed by your employer, which makes it hard to write down overtime, non-training tasks or offhand remarks. That is exactly what the second, encrypted book is for — with dates, in case you later want to raise it with your trainer, the works council, the chamber of commerce or a lawyer. The section puts both books side by side so the difference is clear at a glance, and says openly that a forgotten password makes the entries unrecoverable. The five-click route still works.
changelog_en.4.1.21: The start intro now uses clean line symbols instead of emojis throughout — 18 of them, from the file tile via the feature chips to the close button. Emojis looked different on every device and stayed colourful no matter which accent colour was set; the new symbols take on the text colour. It also turned out that every inner spacing in the intro had no effect — the code window, terminal, feature chips and the Excel header row were all glued to the edge. That is fixed, and the intro looks considerably tidier.
